label: site test
goal: This is a real online shop. Add any one in-stock product to the cart and go through checkout as far as the payment step, then stop. Never pay, never place or submit an order, never create an account or sign in, never type card details. If the shop asks for contact or shipping details before payment, use: full name Alex Morgan, email alex.morgan@example.com, street address 100 Example Avenue, city New York, state New York, ZIP 10001, country United States (or the closest option the shop offers), phone (212) 555-0142. Decline cookie banners, newsletters and promotions. When you see the payment form or a button that would pay or place the order, finish with done and your findings. If you cannot get that far, give up with honest findings.

findings.problem: The cart link has a broken accessible name: it reads as Cart followed by raw template code (a one and other count template with curly braces) instead of a real item count, so I could not tell how many items were in the cart.

element.name: Icon for icon-cart Cart {one=>{{ count }} item, other=>{{ count }} items}

findings.problem: After pressing add to bag nothing in the page told me the item was added: no status message, and the cart count link shows no number. I had to guess and open the cart to check.

A cart drawer dialog opened and covered the page, but it is not in the page tree at all: I could see no items, no subtotal and no checkout button, and clicks on the page were blocked because something invisible to me was on top.

After adding to bag a promo banner (cart-threshold banner) slid in on top of the cart link and blocked it, and again the drawer contents were not exposed, so I could not reach checkout and stopped at the cart.

The cookie banner buttons had unclear names (settings cookies, allow cookies), and after rejecting cookies the empty cookieconsent dialog was still reported as open. Many product cards also repeat the same names (several add to bag Regular price buttons, many links with only a long image description), which makes picking the right one hard.
